A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A-D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A-C report original simulation results, ablations, qualitative rollouts, and failure analyses on Libero, Meta-World, Calvin, and iTHOR.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds a test of policy robustness to video-model sampling rates in Appendix A.9.

M1.justification: The policy architectures, hindsight learning, action chunking, and periodic random exploration are retained. Algorithm 1 now includes the periodic random-exploration branch already described in v1 Section 3.2. The added implementation details do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight Libero, six Meta-World, four Calvin, and twelve iTHOR tasks. Appendix A.9 varies video-model configurations on existing Libero tasks without adding datasets, environments, or task requirements.

E2.justification: Comparator membership remains unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including BC, GCBC, their diffusion-policy variants, SuSIE, AVDC, and DrQ+LIV where originally evaluated. The new sampling-rate study compares configurations of the proposed approach.

E3.justification: Appendix A.9 adds a controlled evaluation that fixes the policy trained with a seven-frame video model and substitutes five- through nine-frame video models at test time, keeping video-model size fixed. Existing protocols are retained; the additional settings in Appendix D are disclosures rather than demonstrated revisions to earlier experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.9 adds a focused robustness study asking whether a fixed policy tolerates different test-time video sampling rates. This is distinct from the retained video-horizon ablation in A.3. Existing ablations and failure analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The existing ± reporting format and A.1's averaging over five checkpoints are retained. Table 12 extends the same reporting format to new results without adding seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: New Table 12 reports fixed-policy results under altered test-time sampling rates. Six-frame models achieve scene averages of 47.8±6.2 and 67.4±9.5, versus 42.2±8.9 and 62.0±8.7 for seven frames. These are additional experimental conditions, not revised same-setting benchmark scores. Existing Tables 1-11 and qualitative findings are retained.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(3), the learning objective, and the action-sampling formulations are unchanged. No substantive mathematical definitions, assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, listed contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about grounding video models through self-supervised exploration, action chunking, and random bootstrapping, with performance competitive with supervised behavior-cloning baselines.

C2.justification: Appendix A.9 attributes sampling-rate robustness to exploration training and extends the existing model-capacity explanation to the six-frame performance peak. Section 4.1 also replaces a speculative zero-shot-generalization remark with an explicit description of video-demonstration training and self-supervised policy training. Existing failure analyses and applicability limitations largely remain.

D1.justification: v1 leaves central exploration settings largely unspecified. New Appendix D.3-D.4 and Tables 15-16 disclose warm-start steps, episode counts and lengths, random-action chunk sizes, exploration frequency, FIFO replay capacities and sharing, action bounds, and success/termination rules. Together with the clarified pseudocode, this substantially expands reproducibility information without establishing that the underlying experiments changed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Luo et al. (2024), 'Text-aware diffusion for policy learning,' to the discussion of video models as reward functions and to the bibliography. The broader positioning relative to prior work remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes include local wording corrections, a shortened Section 3.1 heading, revised discussion prose, the ICLR 2025 publication header, and additional appendix subsections. The main narrative and section ordering remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 12, 15, and 16, expands Algorithm 1 and the Figure 2 caption, and makes limited caption and layout adjustments. The original hyperparameter Tables 12-13 become Tables 13-14. Existing figures retain their visual content, with modest relocation and reflow.

improvement.justification: The clarified algorithm and exploration settings make the method easier to reproduce, while Appendix A.9 provides a useful controlled robustness test. These yield a limited net improvement to an otherwise stable paper. The gains are tempered by unequal-length Calvin action-bound vectors in Table 16 and broad robustness wording despite substantial task-level variation in Table 12.
